verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly's documentation index lists a first-party "Code references" feature. Independent users confirm it answers "where is this flag used in code?" and that LaunchDarkly flags unused or stale flags, including flags only ever evaluated to the default or to one outcome, with temporary/permanent marking to manage flag tech debt. First-party evidence is only a doc title, and nothing shows a workflow that drives actual removal of flags from the codebase. missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on stale-flag detection and code-reference scanning setup, evidence of a cleanup/removal workflow (e.g., archival prompts or automated removal PRs).

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can find stale flags and code references so temporary flags actually get removed from the codebase

citations.quote: LaunchDarkly even has a product feature that does this, called 'Code References.'
spotting unused flags, flags only ever evaluated to the default, and flags only ever evaluated to one outcome
flag usage analytics plus temporary/permanent marking to manage flag tech debt
